title: Priyanka Chopra Just Became India's Third Most Valuable Celebrity. She Hasn't Made a Hindi Film in Seven Years.
excerpt: Fortune India's first-ever celebrity valuation puts a Bollywood exile on the cover — and the math behind her brand empire says more about the industry than any box office number.
body:
Here is the image Fortune India chose for its June 2026 cover: **Priyanka Chopra Jonas**, chin tilted, eyes steady, draped in the kind of quiet authority that makes jewellery campaigns redundant. No film poster behind her. No release date stamped across the bottom. Just a woman whose commercial value now exceeds every actress in the country — and most of the men.

The numbers landed this week. Fortune India, in partnership with global brand consultancy **Interbrand**, published the first-ever **Most Valuable Celebrities 2026** ranking — a study that puts a price on what a famous face is actually worth to the brands it endorses and the industries it touches. The top three get standalone covers.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=ttQaw7tPFBc</youtube>


**Virat Kohli** leads the list. **Shah Rukh Khan** is second. Priyanka is third.

She is the only woman on any of the three covers.

## The Absentee Queen

The most striking detail isn't her rank — it's the asterisk next to her filmography. Priyanka Chopra Jonas has not released a Hindi film in India since **The Sky Is Pink** in October 2019. That's nearly seven years. In an industry that forgets you between Fridays, she has maintained her grip on the Indian imagination by doing something deceptively simple: she stopped needing Bollywood.

Her portfolio reads like a Fortune 500 annual report. Global Ambassador for **Bvlgari** since August 2021. Global Ambassador for **Bentley Motors** since April 2026. Executive producer across multiple international projects. And, increasingly, the kind of cultural diplomat India didn't know it needed — someone whose face sells equally in Mumbai and Manhattan.

The full top ten tells its own story: Kohli, SRK, Priyanka, **MS Dhoni**, **Ranveer Singh**, **Akshay Kumar**, **Amitabh Bachchan**, **Sachin Tendulkar**, **Alia Bhatt**, and **Allu Arjun**. Only two women in the top ten. Priyanka outranks every other actress — including Alia, who has been omnipresent on Indian screens — by a significant margin.

## Varanasi Calls

The timing of this ranking is particularly interesting because Priyanka is, at this very moment, deep in production on a film that could redefine her Indian chapter entirely. She's currently shooting **S.S. Rajamouli's** epic action-adventure **Varanasi**, produced in IMAX format, alongside **Mahesh Babu** and **Prithviraj Sukumaran**.

She plays **Mandakini**. The film is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on **April 7, 2027**.

If the name Rajamouli doesn't immediately explain why this matters, consider: the man made **Baahubali** and **RRR**. He doesn't make films — he makes events. And he chose Priyanka for a project that's been in development for years, which suggests he sees something in her that a regular commercial hit machine can't replicate.

For the Indian diaspora, this is the most tantalising development in years. Priyanka has always been the celebrity who made NRIs feel *seen* — someone who didn't just visit Hollywood but colonised it, who walked Met Galas and UN assemblies with the same ease, who married into American royalty without losing a syllable of her Indianness. A Rajamouli film with her in it is practically a diaspora holiday.

## The Brand Is the Career

What the Fortune India ranking reveals is a truth the entertainment industry has been slow to admit: the biggest stars are no longer the ones who deliver the biggest opening weekends. They're the ones who've become brands unto themselves — whose endorsement value, cultural capital, and global recognition have decoupled from the box office entirely.

Priyanka hasn't needed a hit in India to stay at the top. She's needed Bvlgari, Bentley, Netflix, Citadel, and her own production house. The films are almost incidental — a luxury rather than a necessity.

> "My queen @madhuridixitnene, always the scene stealer and the phenomenon @tripti_dimri" — Priyanka Chopra Jonas on Instagram, reviewing Maa Behen

Even her social media presence this week carried that trademark blend of generosity and dominance. She used her platform to celebrate **Maa Behen**, calling **Madhuri Dixit** her "queen" and labelling **Triptii Dimri** a "phenomenon." It's the kind of gesture that costs nothing and earns everything — the reigning queen knighting the next generation.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs who've watched the Indian entertainment landscape increasingly fragment between theatrical, OTT, and social media, Priyanka's position on this list is oddly reassuring. She represents the idea that Indian stardom can transcend geography, platform, and even the industry that created it.

Fortune India valued her not by her films but by her *influence* — and in 2026, influence is the only currency that doesn't depreciate between releases.

The cover is out. Varanasi is shooting. And somewhere between a Bvlgari campaign and an IMAX set, Priyanka Chopra Jonas is doing what she's always done best: making the rest of the list look like it's playing catch-up.
